Explicit 司馬懿 is linked to retrospective 宣王 and 武帝受禪…宣皇帝; this directly bridges the root’s Emperor Xuan reference under Emperor Wu.
The opening genealogy explicitly equates 宣皇帝 with 懿, surname 司馬 and courtesy 仲達. This is the named Sima Yi in the root cluster, not a title-only match.
宣帝 refuses 魏武 through feigned paralysis and fathers Jingdi/Wendi; the named opening biography and later sons Shi/Zhao identify the same Sima Yi.
Tang ancestral temple succession 宣、光、景、元、神、堯、文武 and relocation of the 宣皇帝 tablet identify a Tang ancestor. This is distinct from the Cao Wei general/Jin ancestor Sima Yi despite the shared 宣帝 title.
The Grand Tutor called 司馬公 entrusts sons Shi and Zhao and then removes Cao Shuang. The Cao Rui deathbed charge explicitly links to the preceding biography.
Returning from Liaodong, he receives Cao Rui’s dying charge with Cao Shuang; son Shi and wife Zhang belong to the same continuing Sima Yi biography.
The Jin songs identify 宣帝 by service to Wei, execution of Meng Da, opposition to Zhuge Liang and defeat of Gongsun. These specific campaigns bridge directly to the named Sima Yi cluster.
Continuous biography after Cao Cao: Cao Pi deathbed charge, Wuyang marquis, and the execution of Meng Da under 司馬公 agree with the root Sanguozhi Meng Da campaign.
The apparatus explicitly names 司馬懿 and identifies the same 宣帝 and 舞陽宣文侯; variant posthumous wording does not create a second person.
The Wen homecoming with brother Fu and son Shi, followed by the Liaodong victory under 司馬公, continues the same Sima Yi biography.
